---
title: "The Laplace approximation"
execute: {warning: false, message: false}
---

A [generalized linear mixed model](generalized-linear-mixed-models.qmd) contains random effects that are not observed directly. The response likelihood is conditional on their values, and the model assigns those values a population distribution. A likelihood for the observed responses must thus average over every possible random-effect value.

This integral usually has no elementary form for a logistic mixed model. The **Laplace approximation** replaces the log integrand with a quadratic near its highest point. We expose that computation with one participant intercept from the SuperTelicity release introduced on the GLMM page.

## Why the integral appears

For participant $p$, let $\mathbf y_p$ denote the binary preposition choices and $b_p$ the participant intercept. Conditional on $b_p$, the participant likelihood is

$$
p(\mathbf y_p\mid b_p,\boldsymbol\beta).
$$

The group model supplies the density $f_B(b_p\mid\tau)$. The observed-data contribution is

$$
p(\mathbf y_p\mid\boldsymbol\beta,\tau)
=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}
p(\mathbf y_p\mid b_p,\boldsymbol\beta)
f_B(b_p\mid\tau)\,db_p.
$$

Integration adds support over every intercept value. Selecting only the best-fitting intercept would omit uncertainty about that latent value.

## Expanding the log integrand

Define

$$
h(b)
=\log p(\mathbf y_p\mid b,\boldsymbol\beta)
+\log f_B(b\mid\tau).
$$

Let $\widehat b$ maximize $h(b)$. At the mode,

$$
h'(\widehat b)=0.
$$

The second-order Taylor expansion is

$$
h(b)
\approx h(\widehat b)
+h'(\widehat b)(b-\widehat b)
+\frac{1}{2}h''(\widehat b)(b-\widehat b)^2.
$$

The first-derivative term vanishes at the mode. Writing

$$
H=-h''(\widehat b)>0
$$

gives

$$
h(b)
\approx h(\widehat b)-\frac{H}{2}(b-\widehat b)^2.
$$

Exponentiating produces a normal-shaped approximation whose integral is

$$
\int \exp\{h(b)\}\,db
\approx
\exp\{h(\widehat b)\}
\sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{H}}.
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\log L
\approx h(\widehat b)
+\frac{1}{2}\log(2\pi)
-\frac{1}{2}\log H.
$$

The height records support at the conditional mode. The curvature records how quickly support falls away from it.

## Constructing the SuperTelicity integrand

The complete teaching GLMM has participant, verb, and sentence intercepts. To make the integral one-dimensional and visible, this page fits a declared computational restriction with only the participant intercept.

```{r}
#| label: supertelicity-laplace
library(lme4)
library(ggplot2)

supertelicity <- read.csv("data/supertelicity/supertelicity-cloze.csv")
supertelicity$participant_id <- factor(supertelicity$participant_id)
supertelicity$verb_type <- factor(
  supertelicity$verb_type,
  levels = c("manner", "result")
)
supertelicity$contentfulness <- factor(
  supertelicity$contentfulness,
  levels = c("contentful", "bleached", "templatic")
)
contrasts(supertelicity$verb_type) <- contr.sum(2)
contrasts(supertelicity$contentfulness) <- contr.sum(3)

fit <- glmer(
  prep_in ~ verb_type * contentfulness +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = supertelicity,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  nAGQ = 1L,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

participant_sizes <- sort(table(supertelicity$participant_id))
selected_participant <- names(participant_sizes)[
  ceiling(length(participant_sizes) / 2)
]
participant_data <- supertelicity[
  supertelicity$participant_id == selected_participant,
]

fixed_matrix <- model.matrix(
  delete.response(terms(fit, fixed.only = TRUE)),
  participant_data
)
fixed_location <- drop(fixed_matrix %*% fixef(fit))
participant_sd <- attr(
  VarCorr(fit)$participant_id,
  "stddev"
)[[1L]]

log1pexp <- function(x) {
  pmax(x, 0) + log1p(exp(-abs(x)))
}

log_integrand <- function(b) {
  bernoulli_part <- sum(
    participant_data$prep_in * (fixed_location + b) -
      log1pexp(fixed_location + b)
  )
  normal_part <- dnorm(
    b,
    sd = participant_sd,
    log = TRUE
  )
  bernoulli_part + normal_part
}

mode_result <- optimize(
  function(b) -log_integrand(b),
  interval = c(-6 * participant_sd, 6 * participant_sd)
)
conditional_mode <- mode_result$minimum
mode_probability <- plogis(fixed_location + conditional_mode)
curvature <- sum(mode_probability * (1 - mode_probability)) +
  1 / participant_sd^2
```

The selected participant has `r nrow(participant_data)` observed trials. This count and every likelihood quantity below come from the release.

## Comparing the exact integral with its local approximation

Numerical integration is stabilized by subtracting the log integrand at the mode before exponentiation.

```{r}
#| label: supertelicity-laplace-summary
log_height <- log_integrand(conditional_mode)

centered_integral <- integrate(
  function(b) {
    vapply(
      b,
      function(value) {
        exp(log_integrand(value) - log_height)
      },
      numeric(1)
    )
  },
  lower = -Inf,
  upper = Inf,
  rel.tol = 1e-11
)$value

exact_log_integral <- log(centered_integral) + log_height
laplace_log_integral <- log_height +
  0.5 * log(2 * pi) -
  0.5 * log(curvature)

laplace_summary <- data.frame(
  participant_id = selected_participant,
  trials = nrow(participant_data),
  conditional_mode = conditional_mode,
  negative_second_derivative = curvature,
  exact_log_integral = exact_log_integral,
  laplace_log_integral = laplace_log_integral,
  laplace_minus_exact = laplace_log_integral - exact_log_integral
)
laplace_summary
```

The small difference is an empirical computation diagnostic for these observed trials. It is not an invented likelihood example and does not guarantee equal accuracy for every participant or for the higher-dimensional crossed model.

```{r}
#| label: plot-laplace
intercept_grid <- data.frame(
  participant_intercept = seq(
    conditional_mode - 4 / sqrt(curvature),
    conditional_mode + 4 / sqrt(curvature),
    length.out = 240L
  )
)
intercept_grid$exact <- vapply(
  intercept_grid$participant_intercept,
  log_integrand,
  numeric(1)
) - log_height
intercept_grid$quadratic <- -0.5 * curvature *
  (intercept_grid$participant_intercept - conditional_mode)^2

plot_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    participant_intercept = intercept_grid$participant_intercept,
    relative_log_integrand = intercept_grid$exact,
    curve = "Exact log integrand"
  ),
  data.frame(
    participant_intercept = intercept_grid$participant_intercept,
    relative_log_integrand = intercept_grid$quadratic,
    curve = "Local quadratic"
  )
)

ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(
    x = participant_intercept,
    y = relative_log_integrand,
    linetype = curve
  )
) +
  geom_line(color = "#1F5A85", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Participant random intercept",
    y = "Log integrand relative to its mode",
    linetype = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

The approximation is a computational method, not a new response model. It does not add a predictor, repair a missing random slope, or make an inappropriate link valid. It tends to be most accurate when the integrand is concentrated and roughly symmetric near its mode; sparse groups, rare responses, boundary variances, or strong asymmetry may make the local quadratic less adequate.

The one-intercept restriction exists only to expose the calculation. The crossed participant, verb, and sentence GLMM remains the scientific teaching model for SuperTelicity.
